title: Impact of 2003 Dividend Tax Cut on Corporate Dividend Payouts

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with two-way (firm and year) fixed effects, supplemented by an event-study robustness check.  

Why DID?  
• We have a clear treatment group (firms highly exposed to the 2003 cut, treated = 1) and a control group (low exposure, treated = 0).  
• We observe them before (post = 0) and after (post = 1) the policy. The interaction treat_x_post is the standard DID term.  

Key assumptions  
1. Parallel-trends: absent the tax cut, the average log-dividend trajectories of treated and control firms would have moved in parallel.  
2. No differential shocks coinciding exactly with treatment that affect only the treated group’s dividends.  
3. Stable unit treatment value (no spill-overs across firms).

An event-study (leads/lags) will visually and formally probe the parallel-trend assumption.  

---

## 2. R Code
```r
############################################################
# Impact of 2003 Dividend Tax Cut on Dividend Payouts
# -----------------------------------------------------
# Required packages:
#   install.packages(c("tidyverse","fixest","modelsummary"))
############################################################
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)
library(modelsummary)

# 1. Read data -------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s33_data.csv",
               col_types = cols())   # automatic type detection

# Quick sanity check
print(head(df, 10))

# 2. Baseline DID: two-way FE ---------------------------------------------
did_twfe <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
                  cluster = ~unit_id,
                  data = df)

cat("\n=== Baseline DID result ===\n")
etable(did_twfe, se = "cluster")

# 3. Event-study (leads/lags) ---------------------------------------------
# We create a relative‐year variable centred on the first post year (=0 in 2003->2004).
# period is already numeric and 3 = 2003, 4 = 2004 etc.  We assume period 3 is 2003.
df <- df %>% mutate(rel_year = period - 3)

# Sun & Abraham style event study: leads −4…−1, lags 0…+4 (0 is first treated year).
es_mod <- feols(y ~ sunab(treated, rel_year, ref = -1) | unit_id + period,
                cluster = ~unit_id,
                data = df)

cat("\n=== Event-study estimates (Sun & Abraham) ===\n")
iplot(es_mod, ref.line = 0, xlab = "Years relative to 2003 cut",
      ylab = "Log-dividend effect")

# 4. Robustness checks -----------------------------------------------------
# (i) Firm-specific linear trends
df <- df %>% group_by(unit_id) %>% mutate(firm_trend = period - mean(period)) %>% ungroup()
did_trend <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post + firm_trend | unit_id + period,
                   cluster = ~unit_id,
                   data = df)

# (ii) Placebo test: pretend the cut happened two years earlier (period<=1 as 'post')
df_plac <- df %>% mutate(post_placebo = ifelse(period >= 2, 1, 0),
                         treat_x_post_pb = treated * post_placebo)
plac_mod <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post_pb | unit_id + period,
                  cluster = ~unit_id,
                  data = df_plac)

cat("\n=== Robustness table ===\n")
modelsummary(list("Baseline DID" = did_twfe,
                  "Firm trends"  = did_trend,
                  "Placebo"      = plac_mod),
             stars = TRUE,
             output = "markdown")

# 5. Print the main coefficient clearly -----------------------------------
coef_main  <- coef(did_twfe)["treat_x_post"]
se_main    <- se(did_twfe)["treat_x_post"]
ci_lower   <- coef_main - 1.96*se_main
ci_upper   <- coef_main + 1.96*se_main

cat("\n------------------------------------------------------------\n")
cat("Effect of dividend tax cut on log-dividends (treated x post):",
    round(coef_main, 3), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(ci_lower, 3), ",", round(ci_upper, 3), "]\n")
cat("------------------------------------------------------------\n")
```

---

## 3. Expected Findings  
Economic intuition: By lowering the shareholder-level tax on dividends, the 2003 act made dividend distributions more attractive. Firms whose investor bases benefited most (highly exposed) should have increased payouts relative to less-exposed firms.  

Sign: Positive.  

Magnitude: A log-dividend coefficient between +0.10 and +0.25 (≈ 10-25 % larger payouts) is plausible, in line with existing literature (e.g., Chetty & Saez 2005). The robustness checks should show a vanishing placebo effect and stable positive estimates once firm trends are added, reinforcing causal interpretation.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log dividend payouts before and after 2003 between treated and untreated firms.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Firms with higher exposure to the dividend tax cut reduced their dividend payouts.
